citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shanghai AI Laboratory)
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
name: MMStar
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each sample was reviewed by three human experts during the manual review process.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom internal review process by three domain experts (no external crowdsourcing platform mentioned)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After automated coarse filtering, three human experts conducted manual review to ensure: (1) each sample's answer is based on understanding visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities. To expedite selection, samples were split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final selection of 1,500 samples considered both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark was specifically designed to mitigate two biases prevalent in existing benchmarks: (1) visual-unnecessary samples where answers can be inferred from text alone or world knowledge embedded in LLMs; (2) unintentional data leakage where evaluation samples appear in LLM/LVLM training data. The automated filtering and manual review process was designed to minimize these biases. The paper notes that existing benchmarks like ScienceQA and AI2D have abnormal LLM hit rates of 57.2% and 46.2% respectively, indicating severe visual-independence bias.
rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from six existing benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) using an automated pipeline. Two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (sizing 20B or larger, including LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) served as inspectors to filter out samples answerable without visual input. Samples with hit counts of two or fewer (i.e., around 75% of LLM inspectors fail) were retained, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples. Three human experts then conducted manual review to select 1,500 final high-quality samples.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples sourced from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED-Image, AI2D-Test, ScienceQA-Test, MMBench-EN-Dev, MathVista-Mini, and MMMU-Val. The initial pool comprised 22,401 samples across these benchmarks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that even the best model (GPT-4V high-resolution) scores under 60% on average, suggesting the benchmark is challenging. The paper also acknowledges plans to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set in the future, implying the current 1,500-sample version has limited scale. The benchmark is derived from existing benchmarks and thus inherits some characteristics of those source datasets.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied: eight LLMs (2 closed-source: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro; 6 open-source: InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B) evaluated each sample; open-source LLMs used a 2-shot in-context inference strategy. Samples with more than 2 LLM hits (i.e., answerable by more than 2 of 8 LLMs without visual input) were excluded. The pool was reduced from 22,401 to 11,607 samples. All questions were converted into multiple-choice format.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states: "In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM's and LVLM's training corpora."
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to provide a more accurate and fair evaluation platform for LVLMs, addressing misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains caused by visual-unnecessary samples and data leakage. This could help the research community make more informed decisions about LVLM development and avoid being misguided by inflated benchmark scores. The paper proposes two metrics (multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage) to enable fairer comparisons between models.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the multi-modal capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs), specifically assessing visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal reasoning across 6 core capability dimensions (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes. Also used with two proposed metrics (multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage) to measure data leakage and actual performance gain from multi-modal training.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as automated inspectors for visual dependency and data leakage filtering: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source); InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B (open-source). Additionally, 16 leading LVLMs (including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series) were used to gauge sample difficulty and split samples into four difficulty levels.
